tasks.title: Give each support card its own portrait, not two shared ones
tasks.why: MEASURED, HudText.cs:87-90 with hud.png's SUPPORT row: the six support cards the HUD offers share two pictures. CREEP returns portrait "HeBarrage", the same as BARRAGE; STRAFE and BEAM return "HeBarrage" too; SMOKE returns "ChlorineGas", the same as GAS. Only Portraits/HeBarrage.png, ChlorineGas.png and ParaDrop.png exist, and UnitLook.cs:247 falls every other ability back to HeBarrage. In hud.png the SUPPORT row reads as six near-identical grey plates. Arming a gas cloud, a smoke line, a strafing run and a walking barrage are four different decisions with four different tips (HudText.cs:68-71), and the card art tells a player nothing apart; under the clock he picks by hotkey or by guess. It is the clearest unfinished surface in the first-assault frame.
tasks.done_when: An EditMode test walks the six abilities in HudView.SupportAbilities plus HeBarrage and ChlorineGas, asserts HudText.Support(id).Portrait is distinct for each, and asserts each returned name has both a .tw-portrait-<name> rule in dustfront.components.uss and a file in Assets/_Project/UI/Skin/Portraits/; it fails today on CreepingBarrage, SmokeScreen, StrafeRun and Beam.

tasks.title: Label the men gauge on screen; it is the only losing signal
tasks.why: TWO-VIEW, hud.png top-left against the probe row "tick 1761 t0 0 fz -99999.0 t1 2 fz 173.6": at the moment the player's whole army was dead the HUD showed a small unlabelled icon and "0 vs 2", and nothing else on screen moved - the OBJECTIVES panel still read the six opening rows, because across three full matches no objective was ever contested (prog 0, cap 255 at every read from tick 0 to 5559). The gauge's heading "MEN" exists only as a hover tip (HudController.cs:175), and a player in a fight does not hover. So the owner's question - can a player tell who is winning and why - answers no on the strongest state the game has: being wiped out reads as a 0 beside an icon he has never been told the meaning of.
tasks.done_when: An EditMode test loads BattleHud.uxml and asserts the men gauge carries a visible on-screen label element reading MEN (not only a tooltip), and that the gauge takes a distinct class when the player's side is at zero; plus a HudCapture.Shoot at a tick where one side has 0 alive shows both.
